summary: Finalized invoice contains negative usage line and missing promo credit after mid-cycle coupon reversal
description:
Issue summary:
Customer was issued a mid-cycle coupon reversal (promo code REACT-30) on 2026-03-11. Invoice for billing period 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-12 finalized on 2026-03-12 and shows: a negative usage line (-1,234 tokens, treated as refund) labelled 'promo-reversal-adjustment' and no corresponding coupon credit line. Customer expects the canceled coupon to produce a single negative credit adjustment, not a phantom usage line; net owed should have been unchanged after reversal.

Impact:
- Customer BrightMap Analytics reports their finalized invoice shows an unexpected negative usage line and is short the expected promo credit. They are concerned about accounting and tax reporting.

Timeline / Background:
- 2026-03-10: Promo REACT-30 applied to account for a trial campaign.
- 2026-03-11 08:22 UTC: Customer requested cancellation of promo; support issued coupon reversal request.
- 2026-03-11 08:23 UTC: Billing service enqueued coupon-reversal postback.
- 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC: Hourly metering run and invoice finalization job executed for customer.
- 2026-03-12 02:05 UTC: Delayed postback processed by reconciler, created a negative usage adjustment record, and did not attach an invoice credit line.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Identify customer org ID (provided separately).
2) Re-run invoice finalization for 2026-03-12 in staging with replayed postbacks with original timing (simulate delayed postback after finalization).
3) Observe line items produced by invoice-compiler service and compare to expected credit memo flow.

Observed behavior:
- Invoice-compiler produced a negative usage line item labeled 'promo-reversal-adjustment' with delta -$12.34 and no separate 'promo credit' invoice line.
- Finance dashboard shows mismatch between postback audit and invoice ledger.

Expected behavior:
- Coupon reversal should create either a single credit memo line associated to the invoice or be deferred to the next invoice depending on the reversal timestamp, but not create a phantom negative usage line on a finalized invoice without an accompanying credit memo.

Logs / evidence:
- Billing reconciler log excerpts (2026-03-12 02:04:57 UTC): "Processed reversal postback for promo REACT-30; marking adjustment type=credit_memo if invoice_open else queue_next; final action=usage_adjustment"
- Invoice-compiler trace ID: invoicectl-20260312-9f2a (attached).
- Customer-provided screenshot of finalized invoice (attached).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Locate org for BrightMap Analytics. 2) Replay the coupon reversal postback with original timestamp after invoice finalization. 3) Run invoice-compiler against the same DB state and note generated line items. 4) Compare ledger entries created by billing-reconciler and invoice-compiler logs.

comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Opening ticket with billing; customer is on enterprise plan and requests a corrected invoice or clear audit trail for tax accounting.

Marco Ruiz (Billing): Investigating reconciler logs and invoice-compiler behavior, reproduced with local replay. Suspect a path where delayed postbacks are treated as usage adjustments instead of credit memos when invoice state is 'finalized'.
SRE (Elena Gomez): Confirmed invoice-compiler accepts 'adjustment_type' flag but found a code path that maps null->usage_adjustment; will add more logging and a unit test.

Finance (Tom Nguyen): Customer requires a credit memo if charge reversed; if we cannot retroactively modify finalized invoice we should issue a separate credit memo and notify customer with tax-friendly documentation.
Customer (BrightMap - Rachel Li): We need confirmation by end of day that either invoice will be reissued or a documented credit memo will be issued for our accounting team.
investigation_notes: Reproducer: replaying postback after invoice finalization consistently produces usage_adjustment line. Root cause hypothesis: when reconciler processes reversal and sees invoice state 'FINALIZED', it should create a credit_memo record on a future invoice but a missing adjustment_type field in the postback payload causes fallback mapping to usage_adjustment. Found code at billing/reconciler/processor.go: mapAdjustmentType(payload.Adjustment) where nil -> USAGE_ADJUSTMENT. PR to add safeguard and explicit mapping created: GH #6767. Need to confirm behavior for already-finalized invoices per accounting policy. Also verify processing window ordering: hourly-run vs postback queue consumer concurrency race.
resolution: Partial workaround applied: billing ops scheduled a manual credit memo to BrightMap for amount $12.34 and flagged account for corrected tax documentation. Finance will create credit memo reference CM-2026-03-12-78 and send to customer. Engineering PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6767) created to enforce adjustment_type mapping; SRE will add a guard to ensure reconciler queues late postbacks to 'deferred_credit' queue rather than applying usage adjustments to finalized invoices. Final fix target: next weekly billing patch (2026-03-18). Follow-up: confirm credit memo posted and customer notified, and add an alert on reconciler postback->usage_adjustment spikes.
next_steps: 1) Finance to issue credit memo and notify customer (TODAY). 2) Engineering deploy PR to staging and run full reconciliation smoke tests (48 hours). 3) Add reconciler alert and unit test to prevent null adjustment_type mapping. 4) Postmortem/short runbook entry in Confluence for handling late promo reversals.
follow_up_actions:
- Send credit memo CM-2026-03-12-78 to BrightMap and confirm receipt.
- Deploy PR #6767 to staging and perform a replay test.
- SRE to add Playbook entry and PagerDuty rule for reconciler anomalies.
- Billing to validate two weeks of invoices for similar anomalies and escalate if recurrence found.
